overview: Mpox is an infectious disease that can cause a painful rash, enlarged lymph nodes, fever, headache, muscle ache, back pain and low energy. Most people fully recover, but some get very sick. Mpox is caused by the monkeypox virus and can be transmitted through close contact with someone who has mpox, with contaminated materials, or with infected animals.
diagnosis: laboratory tests to distinguish mpox from other infections and conditions
treatment: supportive care for symptoms such as pain and fever
close attention to nutrition, hydration, skin care
transmission: close contact with someone who has mpox
contact with contaminated objects such as clothing or linen
animal-to-human transmission through bites or scratches
prevention: avoiding close contact with someone who has mpox
risk_factors: people living with HIV that is not well controlled
complications: corneal infection with loss of vision
key_facts: Mpox is a viral illness caused by the monkeypox virus
There are two distinct clades of the virus: clade I and clade II
A global outbreak of clade IIb began in 2022 and continues to this day
Mpox can be fatal in some cases
